title: Determination of Physical Properties of Undisturbed Soil Samples
author: Spasić, Vacek, et al.
materials: (a)Kopecky steel cylinder (V=100 cm3) with a sample
(b)Laboratory scale (up to 1 kg, min. precision 0.01 g)
(i)Watch glasses (2, one for weighing the sample and one for preventing evaporation)

steps.title: Weigh empty cylinder and glass
steps.instruction: Weigh the empty Kopecký steel cylinder (volume = 100 cm³, without caps) on a laboratory balance and record its mass as GV; also weigh the clean watch glass that will be used later and record its mass as GS.

steps.title: Weigh fresh soil sample
steps.instruction: Place the cylinder containing the fresh (naturally wet) soil sample (caps removed) on a circular piece of filter paper that rests on the watch glass (GS); weigh the assembly and record the mass as GA.

steps.title: Saturate sample by capillary rise
steps.instruction: Set the cylinder on a perforated stand with a filter paper whose sides are dipped in distilled water, cover the cylinder top with a watch glass to prevent evaporation, and allow capillary rise to saturate the sample for 24 h or until the upper surface becomes wet and shiny.

steps.title: Measure fully saturated mass
steps.instruction: After saturation, move the cylinder with its filter paper aside so excess water can drip off; place the cylinder on the same watch glass (GS) and record the mass of the fully saturated sample as GB.

steps.title: Set hour zero for desaturation
steps.instruction: Place the cylinder on a piece of filter paper folded four times, cover with the watch glass, and define this moment as hour zero for subsequent desaturation timing.

steps.title: Weigh after 30‑minute drainage
steps.instruction: Leave the cylinder covered by the watch glass to drain for 30 minutes; then weigh the assembly on the watch glass (GS) and record the mass as GC.

steps.title: Weigh after 2‑hour drainage
steps.instruction: After a total of 2 hours from hour zero (i.e., 90 minutes after the 30‑minute measurement), weigh the cylinder on the same watch glass (GS) and record the mass as GD.

steps.title: Weigh after 24‑hour drainage
steps.instruction: After a total of 24 hours from hour zero, weigh the cylinder on the watch glass (GS) and record the mass as GE.

steps.title: Dry sample to constant mass
steps.instruction: Place the cylinder, the circular filter paper, and the watch glass (GS) in an oven set to 105 °C; dry until a constant mass is obtained and record this final dry mass as GF.

steps.title: Crush and sieve dried soil
steps.instruction: Remove the dried soil from the cylinder, crush it, and sieve the material through a 2.00 mm sieve; keep the sieved soil for the pycnometer determination of particle density.

steps.title: Prepare pycnometer with water
steps.instruction: Fill a pycnometer with distilled water, place it (without cap) in a water bath equilibrated to 20 ± 0.5 °C for 30 minutes, then add the cap, dry the exterior, and weigh; record this mass as PH2O.

steps.title: Boil soil sample in water
steps.instruction: Weigh approximately 10 g of the sieved soil (record the exact mass as n) into a beaker or metal bowl, add a small amount of distilled water, and boil the mixture for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Transfer suspension to pycnometer
steps.instruction: Remove the water from the pycnometer; carefully transfer the boiled soil suspension into the pycnometer, washing the beaker and funnel with distilled water (using a wash bottle) to ensure all soil is transferred.

steps.title: Fill and temper pycnometer
steps.instruction: Fill the pycnometer to the brim with distilled water, place it (without cap) in the 20 ± 0.5 °C water bath for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Weigh pycnometer with soil
steps.instruction: After the bath, install the cap, dry the exterior of the pycnometer and cap, and weigh; record this mass as PZ.

steps.title: Calculate particle density
steps.instruction: Repeat the pycnometer procedure (steps 11‑15) for a second measurement; compute particle density ρz as the average of the two results, ensuring the two values differ by no more than 0.03 g cm⁻³.
